items.description: Life continues in Manipur's relief camps, where the victims of violence confront numerous mental health struggles. items.title: Chancellor Merz backs Ilse Aigner as Germany's first female President
items.author: PRANJAL PANDEY
items.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has endorsed Ilse Aigner for the upcoming presidential election in Germany. Aigner, if elected, would be the first woman to hold this position. Supported by the Christian Democratic Union and the Christian Social Union, she has backing from various political parties. She could succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier, whose presidency ends on March 18. Aigner has previous government experience and a strong political network in Germany.

items.author: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
items.description: Shourya Ambure secured a bronze medal in the women's 100m hurdles at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. This marked India's first track and field medal at the current Youth Olympics edition, showcasing her talent. items.title: Agri loans emerge as biggest asset quality risk for Indian banks
items.description: Agricultural loans in India are currently facing significant asset-quality risks, with bad-loan ratios surpassing other sectors. The gross non-performing asset ratio for agricultural loans is at 5.1%, compared to 1.5% for industry and services. Factors such as a poor monsoon have contributed to this situation, although agricultural bad loans have declined since 2020-21. Various banks have reported increased agricultural loan slippages but maintain a cautious outlook on borrower stress.

items.title: FCNR(B) interest bill to keep dollar hedging costs high
items.description: As a multibillion-dollar FCNR(B) interest bill escalates, Indian banks grapple with increased dollar hedging expenses. Recently, the Reserve Bank of India mandated new reserve prerequisites for forex derivatives, compounding the challenges for banks that must secure cash reserves against these contracts. A significant number of Indian banks are currently without a robust hedging strategy, frequently depending on short-term contracts.

items.title: Stanford scientists build fingernail-sized chip to separate mixed light
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Stanford University researchers have developed a groundbreaking chip that effectively segregates mixed light into its individual components. This novel technology facilitates the analysis of coherence modes of light that were once challenging to identify. Utilizing advanced photonic techniques, the chip can enhance applications in fields like imaging and astronomy, potentially transforming our understanding of microscopic particles and faraway celestial phenomena.
